judgments.note: Neighbors' appeal of a Planning Commission subdivision approval creating seven residential building lots; subdivision creating house lots is new housing per the guide.
The decision states the application is before the Court in this appeal de novo; footnote 12 also refers to the Court in a de novo appeal.
Filing date not stated; the only dated court event is the November 26, 2007 decision, so start and end coincide and duration is unknown.
Each of seven lots is limited to a single-family residence, which suggests seven houses, but no dwelling count is stated and the guide forbids deriving units from lots.
Seven residential building lots stated; Lot 7 is 75.3 acres including conservation land but is still described among the residential building lots, and no existing housing is mentioned on any lot.

Settled on reread: Questions 15 and 16 contest whether the road upgrade causes 'significantly and unreasonably' increased stormwater and sedimentation, an evaluative standard. The second reader's 'fixed rules' covers the other questions.
Stormwater is one of about 18 questions and the only one decided was the fixed road-width rule, so whether the discretionary contention was principal is not shown.

Planning Commission approval is the latest observed authorization; the de novo appeal was pending with partial summary judgment for the applicants. Conditions of the approval are not described, so allowed rather than allowed_with_conditions.
Approved; the decision does not say whether conditions were attached. Page 1 calls it site plan approval, page 5 approval of the subdivision application.
Remaining questions were set for a December 3, 2007 telephone motion hearing; no conclusion observed.
